Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick intro + self-signup path for Dedicated demo

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for signing up and indicating you’re evaluating dedicated capacity for inference. I’m the SDR on your account, looping Ben (AE) and Olga (solutions) in so we can coordinate a technical walkthrough tailored to your throughput needs.

A couple quick items so we come prepared:
- Can you confirm the peak QPS and avg token length (rough ballpark is fine)?
- Is low tail latency (P95) more important than cost, or is there a specific cost target you’re trying to hit?
- Who from your infra team should join (we’ll invite them to the technical slot)?

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30-minute intake (tech + AE) to validate QPS/latency targets and data flow
2) 1-hour dedicated demo with perf run if intake looks clean

If you share two time windows this week I’ll get something on the calendar.

Thanks —
Priyom
SDR, Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Zhang <amelia@quantaai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Black <jordan@quantaai.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick intro + self-signup path for Dedicated demo

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the note. Short answers:
- Peak QPS: ~450 reqs/sec during batch ingestion windows; steady-state ~40 qps
- Typical prompt + context tokens: 300–800, we’re sensitive to P95 <= 250ms for short reqs but can accept higher for long-context batched runs
- I'll bring Jordan (infra lead) to the intake — he’s CC'd.

We actually tried the self-serve instance briefly; looks promising. Two windows this week that work for us: Wed 10/1 11:00–13:00 PT or Thu 10/2 09:00–11:00 PT.

Can Ben or your solutions team confirm you can demonstrate perf under a high-QPS simulated workload?

Best,
Amelia
Head of Applied ML, QuantaAI

Hi Amelia —

Appreciate the details — that QPS profile is exactly the kind of workload our Dedicated customers run. We can absolutely show a perf run that stresses peak QPS and exercises tail latency. For the intake/demo I suggest:

- Intake (30m): Wed 10/1 11:00 PT — confirm data ingress pattern, token distribution, and any SLOs
- Demo (60m): Thu 10/2 09:00 PT — focused perf run with a synthetic load generator, live token/time metrics, and fallback routing walkthrough

Monica (CC) will own the demo orchestration and will send the meeting invite + short pre-demo worksheet to populate (networking, test data, allowed IPs). If you prefer the reverse order (demo first), let us know.

Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Amelia / Jordan —

Thanks — looping in the solutions folks for the intake + orchestration. I attached a short Dedicated_Capacity_Worksheet.xlsx to this thread (fields we need populated ahead of the perf run). A few clarifications from our side so the demo is meaningful:

- For the perf run we’ll simulate the 450 QPS peak with a mix of short (100–400 token) and long (600–1200 token) requests so we exercise both tail latency and KV cache effects.
- If you have any PII in sample prompts, please scrub or provide synthetic samples — we won’t need production data for the demo.
- Network: if you’re behind a proxy or have egress restrictions, add the IP ranges in the worksheet.

Please confirm the intake on Wed 10/1 11:00 PT — I’ll open a 30m slot and include a short pre-read with the worksheet. I also added a calendar link to propose Thu 10/2 09:00 PT for the perf demo.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Capacity_Worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12 KB)
